items.pronunciation_notes: A long uu after an unaspirated त with the tongue on the teeth: tuu, one syllable.

learn.title_en: तू — recognise it, do not use it
learn.explanation_en: तू is the third word for 'you', and it is the one to be careful with. Grammatically it is simple: it takes है, the same form as the third person. Socially it is not. Between very close friends, from a parent to a small child, or in prayer, it is warm. Said to a stranger, a shopkeeper or anyone older, it is an insult. A learner has no reliable way to tell those situations apart, so learn to recognise तू and leave it alone.

examples.note: तू takes है, unlike तुम which takes हो.
Singular agreement throughout, unlike तुम.
Identical in form to वह यहाँ है, which is part of why it feels distancing.

common_error.why_en: तू takes है rather than हो — though the more useful correction is to say तुम or आप instead.

practice.question: तू कहाँ ___?
practice.explanation_en: तू takes है, the same form as a third person singular.

game.explanation_en: तू behaves as a singular and takes है. हो would be right after तुम.

items.pronunciation_notes: The final vowel drops, giving ham in one syllable.

learn.explanation_en: हम is we, and it takes हैं in the present and थे or थीं in the past. There is a regional habit worth knowing about: across much of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, a single speaker uses हम where standard Hindi would use मैं. You will hear it and it is not an error, but keep to मैं yourself and you will always be understood.

examples.note: हम takes हैं, like any plural.
Masculine or mixed groups take -े.
The past takes थे, or थीं for an all-female group.

common_error.why_en: हम is plural, so it takes हैं. हूँ belongs to मैं alone.

practice.question: हम यहाँ ___।
practice.explanation_en: हम is plural, so the verb is हैं.

game.explanation_en: हम is plural and first person, so only हैं fits.

items.pronunciation_notes: Written यह but said 'ye' in almost all ordinary speech, with the ह barely sounded.

learn.title_en: यह — this, and he or she nearby
learn.explanation_en: यह does two jobs at once. It means 'this', and it is also the third person pronoun for someone or something close at hand. Hindi does not separate 'this' from 'he' and 'she' the way English does, and it does not mark gender on the pronoun at all — यह अच्छा है and यह अच्छी है differ only in the adjective. It takes है, and it is written यह but said 'ye'.

examples.note: यह as a demonstrative, standing before a noun.
यह standing alone as the subject.
The same word covers 'this' and 'it'.

common_error.why_en: यह is singular, so a plural noun needs ये instead.

practice.question: यह किताब ___।
practice.explanation_en: यह and किताब are both singular, so the verb is है.

game.explanation_en: यह is singular, so it needs a singular noun and a singular verb.

summary.recap_en: This level added तू, हम and यह. तू is the one to recognise and avoid, हम behaves as a plural, and यह covers both 'this' and a nearby 'he' or 'she'.
summary.next_up_en: Next: वह, ये and वे complete the nine pronouns.

items.pronunciation_notes: Written वह but said 'vo' in almost all ordinary speech, which catches learners who have only seen it written.

learn.title_en: वह — that, and he or she over there
learn.explanation_en: वह is the far counterpart of यह: 'that', and also 'he' or 'she' when the person is not right beside you. Like यह it takes है and marks no gender of its own. And like यह it is written one way and said another — वह comes out as 'vo' in ordinary speech, so a learner who has only read it will not recognise it when it is spoken.

examples.note: वह as a demonstrative before a noun.
The same word doing duty as a pronoun.
वह modifying a noun inside a longer sentence.

common_error.why_en: वह is singular and takes है. वे is the plural form.

practice.question: वह घर बड़ा ___।
practice.explanation_en: घर is singular, so the verb is है.

game.explanation_en: वह is singular, so both the adjective and the verb stay singular.

items.pronunciation_notes: A flat ए with no glide: ye, one syllable — and identical to how यह is usually pronounced.
items.gloss_en: these; they — near; and a respectful singular

learn.title_en: ये — these, and a respectful 'this person'
learn.explanation_en: ये is the plural of यह: 'these', or 'they' for people nearby. It takes हैं. It has a third use worth knowing now: a single person spoken of respectfully takes ये rather than यह, exactly as आप takes हैं. So ये अच्छे हैं can mean 'these are good' or, of one person, 'he is good' said politely — only the situation tells you which.

examples.note: Plural demonstrative with a plural noun.
Standing alone as a plural subject.
Every word in the sentence is plural.

common_error.why_en: ये is plural, so it cannot stand before a singular noun.

practice.question: ये किताबें ___।
practice.explanation_en: ये and किताबें are both plural, so the verb is हैं.

game.explanation_en: ये is plural, so the noun, the adjective and the verb all have to be plural too.

items.pronunciation_notes: Written वे but very often said 'vo', the same as वह, so the spoken singular and plural collapse together.
items.gloss_en: those; they — far; and a respectful singular

learn.explanation_en: वे is the plural of वह: 'those', or 'they' for people further off, and it takes हैं. Like ये it also serves as a respectful singular. There is a practical complication: in ordinary speech वे is usually pronounced exactly like वह, so the difference between singular and plural disappears from the sound entirely and the verb becomes the only thing telling you which was meant.

examples.note: Plural demonstrative, plural verb.
Standing alone as a subject.
The past plural takes थे.

common_error.why_en: वे is plural, so the verb has to be हैं.

practice.question: वे बच्चे छोटे ___।
practice.explanation_en: बच्चे is masculine and plural, so the past form is थे.

game.explanation_en: वे is plural, so only हैं fits.

summary.recap_en: This level completed the nine pronouns with वह, ये and वे. Hindi splits them by distance rather than by gender, and in speech वह and वे collapse into the same sound, leaving the verb to carry the number.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the three words for 'you' as a social scale, and what each one costs you.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words are single syllables and neither carries stress: tuu hai.
items.gloss_en: the तू level — intimate or contemptuous

learn.explanation_en: The three words for 'you' form a scale of social distance, and तू sits at the bottom of it. Parents use it to small children, lifelong friends use it to each other, and it is the form used in prayer. Everyone else hears it as contempt. There is no situation in which a learner needs तू and several in which using it would end a conversation badly, so treat it as read-only: know it when you hear it, never say it.

examples.note: Affectionate from a parent, an insult from a stranger.
Singular agreement all the way through.
The past takes था or थी, exactly like a singular.

common_error.why_en: तू takes है — though the correction a learner actually needs is to switch to तुम or आप.

practice.question: तू यहाँ ___।
practice.explanation_en: तू behaves as a singular, so the past form is था or थी.

game.explanation_en: तू takes है. Being able to recognise this pairing matters more than being able to use it.

items.pronunciation_notes: Both words drop their final vowels and run together easily in speech: tum ho.
items.gloss_en: the तुम level — friends and equals

learn.explanation_en: तुम is the middle of the scale and the one you will use most with people you actually know: friends, siblings, cousins, colleagues of your own age, children who are past being tiny. It takes हो, and its adjectives take plural endings even when you are speaking to one person. Moving from आप to तुम with someone is a small social event, and it is normally the older or more senior person who offers it.

examples.note: The ordinary greeting between friends.
A plural adjective for a single person.
The past takes थे, or थीं for a woman.

common_error.why_en: तुम takes plural agreement, so the adjective is अच्छे even when one person is meant.

practice.question: तुम अच्छे ___।
practice.explanation_en: तुम takes हो, and nothing else does.

game.explanation_en: तुम needs a plural adjective and the verb हो. Only one option has both.

items.pronunciation_notes: Two long vowels then a nasalised one: aap haiṁ, with no n sounded at the end.
items.gloss_en: the आप level — respect and distance

learn.explanation_en: आप is the top of the scale: elders, strangers, teachers, officials, anyone senior, and anyone you have not met before. It takes हैं and थे. For a learner it is the right default almost everywhere, because the cost of being too polite is nothing — at worst someone tells you to relax and use तुम, which is a pleasant thing to be told and a signal you have been accepted.

examples.note: The safe greeting for anyone at all.
Plural agreement, however many people are meant.
The past takes थे, or थीं for a woman.

common_error.why_en: आप takes हैं. Mixing आप with हो sounds like you began respectfully and gave up halfway through.

practice.question: आप कहाँ ___?
practice.explanation_en: आप takes हैं, whether one person or several are meant.

game.explanation_en: आप always takes हैं. हो belongs with तुम and sounds too familiar here.

summary.recap_en: This level set out the three levels of 'you' as a social scale. तू is for reading only, तुम is for people you know, and आप is the learner's default — and each takes its own form of होना.
summary.next_up_en: Next: making the choice, the same scale in the past, and the particle जी.

items.pronunciation_notes: All three are short and unstressed, so in fast speech the pronoun is easy to miss and the verb often gives it away first.

learn.explanation_en: English has one word for 'you' and Hindi has three, so every time you address someone you make a decision English never asked of you. The rule for a learner is short enough to memorise: use आप unless you have been invited to use तुम, and never use तू. Erring upwards is invisible and costs nothing. Erring downwards is not invisible at all.

examples.note: To anyone at all: safe.
To a friend: warm and correct.
To a stranger: an insult.

common_error.why_en: The same question exists at three levels of politeness, and only the top one is safe for a learner to use.

practice.question: ___ कैसे हैं?
practice.explanation_en: हैं points to आप here. तू would need है and तुम would need हो.

game.question_en: Which greeting is safe for a learner to use with a stranger?
game.explanation_en: Only आप is safe with someone you do not know. तुम is correct Hindi but too familiar here, and the तू options are worse.

items.target: तू था / तुम थे / आप थे
items.read_as: tuu thaa / tum the / aap the
items.pronunciation_notes: थे and था differ only in the final vowel, and neither is stressed, so the distinction is easy to lose in fast speech.
items.gloss_en: the same scale in the past

learn.title_en: The same scale in the past
learn.explanation_en: The three levels keep their agreement in the past as well. तू behaves as a singular and takes था or थी. तुम and आप both behave as plurals and take थे or थीं. That means तुम and आप look identical once you reach the verb — the difference between them survives only in the pronoun itself, so dropping the pronoun costs you the politeness along with it.

examples.note: Singular, and feminine.
Plural agreement for one person.
The identical verb, with more respect in the pronoun.

common_error.why_en: आप takes plural agreement, so its past form is थे or थीं and never था.

practice.question: आप यहाँ ___।
practice.explanation_en: आप takes plural agreement, so the past form is थे.

game.explanation_en: तू is the only one of the four that behaves as a singular, so it is the only one that can take था.

items.pronunciation_notes: A single long syllable, unstressed and often run onto the word before it: jii.

learn.explanation_en: जी is added after names and kinship terms to show respect: पिता जी, दादी जी. On its own it is a polite 'yes', and जी हाँ is more formal still. It never changes form and it costs nothing to add, which makes it the cheapest way for a learner to sound courteous without having to get anything else right. Remember that a person spoken of respectfully also takes हैं rather than है.

examples.note: Added to a kinship term, unchanged.
The same particle, and it does not agree with anything.
More formal than हाँ standing on its own.

common_error.why_en: Adding जी marks respect, and a person spoken of respectfully takes हैं rather than है.

practice.question: पिता जी ___।
practice.explanation_en: जी marks respect, and a respected person takes हैं even though only one is meant.

game.explanation_en: The respectful हैं goes with जी, the same way it goes with आप.

summary.recap_en: This level turned the register scale into a decision rule — आप by default, तुम when invited, तू never — and added जी, which extends respect to anyone you name.
summary.next_up_en: Next: यह against वह, ये against वे, and a short conversation in a shop.

items.pronunciation_notes: Said 'ye' and 'vo' in ordinary speech, so listen for the vowel rather than expecting the spelling.
items.gloss_en: near against far, in the singular

learn.title_en: यह and वह — near and far
learn.explanation_en: यह points at what is close and वह at what is further off, which is the same split English makes between 'this' and 'that'. The difference is that Hindi uses these same two words for 'he' and 'she', choosing by distance rather than by gender — so nothing in the pronoun tells you who is being spoken about. Both take है.

examples.note: Something near at hand.
The same kind of object, further away.
Standing alone, with no noun after it.

common_error.why_en: वह is singular, so a plural noun needs वे instead.

practice.prompt_en: Complete the sentence about something close by.
practice.question: ___ किताब है।
practice.explanation_en: किताब is singular and the thing is close by, so the word is यह.

game.explanation_en: किताबें is plural, so it needs a plural demonstrative — वे for something far off.

items.pronunciation_notes: ये is said 'ye' and वे usually 'vo', so वे and वह sound alike and only the verb separates them.
items.gloss_en: near against far, in the plural

learn.title_en: ये and वे — these and those
learn.explanation_en: ये and वे are the plurals of यह and वह, and both take हैं. Both also serve as respectful singulars, which is why ये अच्छे हैं can mean 'these are good' or, of one person, 'he is good' said politely. In speech वे is usually pronounced the same as वह, so the written difference disappears and the verb becomes your only clue to the number.

examples.note: Near, and plural.
Far, and plural.
Or, of one person, 'he is good' said respectfully.

common_error.why_en: A singular noun needs the singular यह.

practice.prompt_en: Complete the sentence about things close by.
practice.question: ___ किताबें हैं।
practice.explanation_en: किताबें is plural and the things are close by, so the word is ये.

game.explanation_en: ये is plural, so both the adjective and the verb have to be plural as well.

items.pronunciation_notes: यह is said 'ye' and क्या runs क straight into य, so the whole question is three quick syllables.
items.setting_en: A customer and a shopkeeper at a small shop

learn.explanation_en: यह क्या है? is the most useful question a beginner owns: point, ask, and take the answer as vocabulary. Swap यह for वह and you are asking about something across the room instead. Watch the shopkeeper's last line in this exchange — he switches to वे because he is pointing at more than one thing, and the verb changes with it.

common_error.why_en: The shopkeeper is pointing at several books, so the demonstrative has to be plural too.

practice.question: वे किताबें ___।
practice.explanation_en: वे and किताबें are both plural, so the verb is हैं.

game.question_en: Listen to the last line. Which word is missing?
game.mask_reason: the plural far demonstrative agreeing with किताबें
game.explanation_en: The books are plural and across the shop, so the demonstrative is वे — far, and plural.

summary.recap_en: This level set the four demonstratives against each other: यह and वह for one thing near or far, ये and वे for several. The shop dialogue puts all four to work, and shows the verb changing along with them.
summary.next_up_en: Next: more on the demonstratives, and then the question words in full.
